subject: Starlane: sudden throughput collapse & elevated 5xx rate — war-room activation
messages:
From: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@starlane.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Starlane SRE <sre@starlane.io>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:34:12 -0700
Subject: Production impact — 5xx spike and throughput drop (US-east)

Marissa —

We're seeing a severe degradation on our integration with Redwood (prod, us-east) starting ~09:05 PDT. Symptoms:
- 5xx/error rate climbed from ~0.3% baseline to ~12% at peak
- End-to-end latency for the primary path jumped from ~220ms -> 1.2s for many requests
- Overall throughput to our model-backed endpoints dropped ~40% despite no traffic changes on our side

Attached is a short snapshot from our telemetry (request IDs + sample traces). We have several customers complaining about timeouts. Can you confirm whether this is a platform issue or something on the model side?

Request IDs: stl-11a2b, stl-11a2c, stl-11a2d
Errors look like: "model invocation 503 / kv cache miss cascade" in the stack traces.

Please escalate — this is customer-impacting.

— Alex Jensen
CTO, Starlane
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@starlane.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:42:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — 5xx spike and throughput drop (US-east)

Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and for including the request IDs. We're activating a focused war-room and will own the response. Summary of next steps from our side:
1) I have looped in infra (Karthik) and CS (Grace).
2) We're pulling the first wave of telemetry now — Karthik, can you confirm whether this is an inference runtime or routing/fanout issue?
3) We'll propose an immediate mitigation (route traffic to the compatible model shard or temporarily widen batching window) and will share an ETA for customer-facing mitigation within 20 minutes.

Alex, can you confirm whether you see any correlating deploys or config changes on your side around 09:00? Also please share the stack traces as plain text if possible (the PNG is helpful but plain logs are easier to search).

I'll post a running minutes doc to the Drive link and put a short executive note to our leadership once we have the mitigation plan.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:58:31 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — quick findings and proposed mitigations

TL;DR: Early signals point to a KV cache eviction storm on the primary inference pool (us-east-1a) coinciding with a spike in long-sequence requests. That caused backend timeouts and backpressure into the batching layer.

What we observed:
- Metric: kv_cache_evictions/s spiked from ~2 -> ~320 starting 09:04
- Concurrent LB queue depth increased by ~3.5x on the affected pool
- Model worker logs show repeated
  "cache-get miss -> cold load -> model init latency >= 900ms"

Immediate mitigations (can be executed in this order):
A) Expand cache retention window on us-east-1a (low risk, config change) — expected improvement in <5m after rollout.
B) Temporarily route 20% of Starlane traffic to the warm-standby pool us-east-1b (compatible model variant). This reduces peak load and isolates the hot path.
C) As a fallback, widen continuous batching max window by 50ms to increase aggregation — small latency tradeoff but reduces per-token overhead.

I will start A) now and open the route change for a manual approval (B). If A) resolves >75% of the error spike, we'll hold off on routing.

Attachments: starlane_snapshot_1100z.png (request-rate + eviction chart)
Operational doc: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/starlane-warroom-20270627

— Karthik Iyer
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@starlane.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 10:12:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact — mitigation & exec status (war-room minute)

Alex — quick update from the war-room: we executed mitigation A) (expanded cache retention) at 09:58 PDT. Early telemetry shows error rate dropping from 12% -> 3.1% in the first four minutes and latency normalizing toward baseline. We're continuing to monitor for stabilization over the next 30 minutes.

If the drop holds, we will NOT do routing B). If we see a re-escalation we will route 20% of traffic to us-east-1b (manual approval needed).

Executive note for your leadership: Rishi and I will prepare a brief (one-slide) incident readout and customer remediation summary after the incident closes. David is available to discuss credits/contract remediation if Starlane requests them.

I'm copying Rishi so leadership is informed of potential downstream customer outreach.

Subject: Re: Production impact — mitigation & exec status (war-room minute)

Marissa — this is excellent, and thank you for the rapid response. We can confirm our side shows the error rate falling in line with your telemetry. No deploys on our side — just a steady production load.

We have one of our SREs standing by to join a short wrap-up call at 14:30 PDT to review root cause and longer-term remedies (cache sizing recommendations and an SLA discussion). Can you confirm a dial-in and whether anyone from product pricing will join (David)?

Appreciate the clear communication — will wait for your readout.

— Alex
